subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should classic voice calls gain a permanent provider-generic sentence-level streaming speech contract, and which provider/carrier combination should define its first supported implementation?
rationale: This changes external plugin speech capabilities and failure semantics across providers and carriers; source inspection cannot safely choose that lasting API boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared additive contract
options.body: Design the provider-generic contract first and implement one live-proven provider/carrier slice with buffered fallback.

options.title: Plugin-local experiment
options.body: Prototype the pipeline privately inside voice-call until live Twilio and Telnyx evidence establishes stable shared semantics.

options.title: Realtime-only direction
options.body: Decline further classic-pipeline investment and direct low-latency callers to supported full-duplex realtime providers.

recommendation.title: Shared additive contract
recommendation.body: Design the provider-generic contract first and implement one live-proven provider/carrier slice with buffered fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans the voice-call architecture, provider integrations, realtime path, and current canonical issue discussion.
